newsitem.title: USA: PrimeStar in tentative deal with News Corp - source.
newsitem.headline: PrimeStar in tentative deal with News Corp - source.

text.p: PrimeStar Partners has reached a tentative agreement for News Corp Ltd to join the satellite-dish TV service as a partner, according to a source close to the matter.
The two sides are continuing their discussions, which were described as fragile and ongoing, and it was possible the deal could still unravel, the source said.
The source said the agreement would call for News to contribute the satellites it controls and other transmission sites in return for a non-voting stake in PrimeStar.

A PrimeStar spokeswoman denied there was any tentative deal. "Discussions are ongoing, but at this point, we have no agreement," the spokeswoman said. "All the partners in PrimeStar are interested in seeing the situation resolved as quickly as possible."
The Wall Street Journal reported earlier Tuesday that News Corp and PrimeStar had reached a deal.
Among the terms still be resolved is how a new venture would be financed, as well as how to phase in new 18-inch dishes to customers now using PrimeStar's 36-inch dishes, the paper said.
PrimeStar partners include Tele-Communications Inc, U S West Media Group, Cox Communications Inc, Comcast Corp, and Time Warner Inc.
Analysts said Murdoch's participation in PrimeStar would calm those on Wall Street who were concerned that a direct broadcast venture by Murdoch would require massive capital expenditures.
"It's scared lots of people," said Stewart Halpern, an analyst at Furman Selz.
Halpern said that the potential deal offers Murdoch an entry into satellite TV, and also gives News Corp an outlet for selling its 20th Century-Fox film and Fox Broadcasting television programming.
"From a strategic point of view it would be quite valuable," Halpern said.
Murdoch's first foray into satellite-TV, a deal to acquire EchoStar Communications Corp, collapsed only weeks after it was announced two months ago.
